text:
maria: Heads-up: ran a long trace on the prod decode service. When requests include structured outputs + function/tool calls we see increased tail latency and a lot more kernel swaps during decode. attaching quick profiler snippets below.

kevin: ugh. same buckets as last week? is this more queue formation or the tool pause resuming? :thinking_face: 

maria: looks like both. batch formation waits longer because of stop-token checks for structured outputs, then when function call arrives we pause and later resume on a different worker/kernel. swap overhead is the killer.

sanjay: can you paste the flame/logs? even tiny numbers help.

maria: sure. simplified extract from a 2000-request sample (timestamps in ms):
```
[request_id=0x4f2] queue_enter=12 queue_hold=45 decode_start=57 tool_pause=120 tool_resume=260 kernel_swap=138 kernel_exec=420 kv_hit_rate=0.62
[request_id=0x9c1] queue_enter=9 queue_hold=30 decode_start=39 tool_pause=100 tool_resume=240 kernel_swap=124 kernel_exec=380 kv_hit_rate=0.88
[request_id=0x2a7] queue_enter=8 queue_hold=6 decode_start=14 no_tool kernel_swap=12 kernel_exec=110 kv_hit_rate=0.95
```
maria: note kernel_swap numbers jump 100+ms when tool pauses cause worker handoff. also batch sizes before pause are ~6, after resume they drop to 1-2 because of affinity loss.

jen: so we get both batching fall-off and a hard kernel swap penalty. Did the kernel selector choose different kernels because sequence length or structured token markers changed?

maria: yeah the selector sometimes picks int8-quantized kernels for short sequences but after a resume the predicted seq distribution changes (tool outputs + function tokens), so scheduler moves to a fallback kernel (kernel_swap). kernel selection cost + reloading KV cache leads to big tail.

kevin: what about keeping the same kernel pinned during a short tool pause (<300ms)? Could we prefer avoiding swap if batch composition is similar?

sanjay: that's what i wanted to test. ran an experiment toggling 'swap-on-pause=false' for pauses < 500ms and increasing soft token_budget_target by 10%. results: median latency unchanged, p95 improved ~12%, p99 improved ~22% — but cost went up slightly due to less-optimal kernel for some long sequences.

maria: experiment logs (condensed):
```
config: swap_on_pause=false; token_budget_target=110%
results: median=43ms (no change) p95=210ms -> 185ms p99=480ms -> 375ms
cost_delta=+3%
note: kv_hit_rate stable, batch_size_after_pause +2.1 avg
```

jen: promising. But application correctness: for structured outputs we rely on stop-token behavior to cut generations. Did disabling swap affect eventual tokenization/stop detection?

maria: no regressions in stop detection on unit tests. The main risk is increased CPU/GPU occupancy because we keep the kernel resident. We need a mechanism to only pin kernels when predicted resume time < threshold and when affinity likelihood > threshold.

kevin: could use a quick affinity predictor: features = {time_in_queue, tokens_emitted, last_msg_has_fn_call, kv_hit_rate_est}. cheap model. Return probability of resume_on_same_worker. if >0.6, pin.

sanjay: exactly. also adjust continuous-batcher to avoid draining a batch if a request looks likely to pause for a function call. i.e., bias batch formation to prefer grouping non-pausing requests and keep a small reserved pool for in-flight resumes.

perf-bot: CI perf-suite: run-1945678 completed. baseline vs experiment: p99 tail reduced 24% for structured-output workloads, no OOMs.

jen: good. next steps: 1) implement cheap affinity predictor + threshold config, 2) add 'pin_on_short_pause' toggle in kernel selector, 3) adjust batcher to reserve N slots for likely resumes, 4) run 48h canary.

maria: i've created a draft PR with the config toggles and a basic affinity model (sigmoid on features). link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7823 . please review quick.

kevin: i'll review today. also add a metric for 'kernel_swap_ms' per-request and an alert if > 80ms p95.

sanjay: and we should capture KV cache cold-start counts when swap happens, add kv_reload_ms metric. that made a big difference in the traces.

maria: agreed. i'll add both metrics and a dashboard widget showing batch_size_before/after pause, kernel_swap_ms, kv_reload_ms. thanks team :thumbsup:
